A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same variance-reduction study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A.1–A.11, including the image-only case studies, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on three textual datasets and text-to-image generation, including per-seed performance, training times, variance measurements, ablations, and generated examples.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices. Their retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: P-POTS's EPR fitting and importance weighting, MIRROR's complementary masks, and ISAD, SyRM, StraTS, and EMA retain the same procedures. The conjectural reinforcement-learning adaptation in A.9 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OpenScience, GSM8K, HiTab, and text-to-image-2M with the same task coverage. The reinforcement-learning extension remains unevaluated in both.

E2.justification: Standard and Clipped training, the auxiliary methods, and the ARM comparators remain unchanged. Table 1 retains Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B-Base, and Llama3.1-8B-Instruct. P-POTS and MIRROR rows incorporated into v2 Table 1 already appeared in v1's corresponding ablation comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix A.7 retains the same splits, preprocessing, learning rate, batch size, training budget, early stopping, and decoding settings. Evaluation still uses pass@1 accuracy for textual tasks and CLIP scores for image generation.

E4.justification: The component ablations, EPR versus degree-7 polynomial comparison, sampler-drift analysis, batch-size analysis, loss curves, and image case studies are retained. Consolidating v1 Table 2 into v2 Table 1 changes their presentation, not the analyses.

E5.justification: Both specify seeds 42, 731, and 20231 and retain the same per-seed and average reporting, including single-seed entries for auxiliary methods. The loss-variance estimator in A.7.2 is unchanged; neither version adds confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched scores, training times, variance values, plots, and generated examples are unchanged. For example, P-POTS+MIRROR's mean accuracies remain 52.53, 60.53, and 67.10 on OpenScience, GSM8K, and HiTab, and its mean image-generation CLIP score remains 34.59.

T1.justification: The decomposition, optimal-sampler derivation, MIRROR variance calculation, and appendix assumptions and proofs are retained. V2 clarifies notation in Eq. 1 and repairs internal equation references, including the unresolved reference in A.5.2, without changing the mathematical arguments.

C1.justification: Both retain the three-source decomposition, six techniques, P-POTS optimality, P-POTS/MIRROR synergy, and improved accuracy and stability as their principal contributions. The conclusion's change from 'training variance' to 'loss variance' clarifies the objective already explicitly identified in v1 Section 2.1.

C2.justification: V2 removes the suggestion that ARM-generated reasoning labels explain MDMs' shorter responses, and drops the explanation that learning easier low-mask-rate cases drives sampler drift toward a U-shape. The decoding-budget explanation, variance-proxy caveat, and limitations concerning adaptive refitting and reinforcement learning remain.

D1.justification: V2's abstract adds a StableDLLM repository address and a promise of future code release; v1 provides no corresponding project-code location. This adds access information without establishing completed release. Implementation settings, data processing, hardware disclosures, and training-time results remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works remain the same after matching bibliographic updates. However, the condensed related-work discussion drops specific criticisms of Xu et al.'s idealized assumptions and Jeha et al.'s performance in high-dimensional nonlinear networks, modestly revising the positioning against prior methods.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially reorganized: related work moves from A.3 to Section 2, while the variance-decomposition discussion moves from Section 2.1 to A.3. Separate experimental setup and results subsections are consolidated, and related-work, interpretation, and case-study paragraphs are condensed. Cross-references and unfinished text are also cleaned up.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a new branded template with different typography, a shaded abstract, running headers and footers, and revised caption styling. V1 Tables 1 and 2 are consolidated, figures and appendix image pairs are enlarged or redistributed, and the appendix variance table spans two pages. The scientific image and plot content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves usability by foregrounding related work, consolidating comparisons, and repairing broken or incorrect proof references while retaining the experimental evidence. The code-release pointer adds useful information but remains a promise. Scientific support is unchanged, and existing overstatements persist: the claimed best-versus-worst separation on OpenScience still conflicts with Table 1's Clipped score of 50.90 versus P-POTS+MIRROR's lowest score of 50.80.
